Nizamuddin Haider with H. N. Nondy ------ For the Appellant

Haran Chandra Daradi ------Appellant
Vs.
Ejhar Molla & ors ------Respondents
full_judgment: 5. When the matter went to appeal the defendants 1 and 2 objected before the court of appeal below stating that the trial court was wrong to observe that the issue on defect of parties was not too much agitated and hence that finding was wrong and the trial court should have dismissed the suit for defect of parties. On appeal, the plaintiff also filed a cross-objection on the ground that the c. s. khatian No. 444 and 929 were wrongly recorded and that the trial court was wrong in holding that Feli Bewa had annas 11 gondas 1 kara 2 kranti shares, claiming plaintiffs 2 and 3 as bonafide transferees and they acquired title also by adverse possession and further that the heirs of Khudiram and Jadu were not necessary parties as their lands were tenanted and their rent receiving interest had been acquired by Government. The court of appeal. below had occasion to examine the relevant khatians of the suit namely khatiati Nos. 444, 929 and 764 which were also examined by me at the time of hearing of this appeal. According to the these khatian Shasi Daradi, son of Jadu Nath Daradi had 2 annas odd share, Khudiram, son of Kartik another recorded tenant had 4 annas and odd share and Jadhunath son of Pitambar as original tenant had 4 annas share which meant Shasi, father of the plaintiff had 1/7th share and other 3 tenants had 2/7th share each in the land. On a reference to khatian No. 929 covering an area of 8.84 it is seen that Jadunath had no possession in the khas land in the khatian. Similar is the case in khatian No. 444. These khatians were accepted by the plaintiff to be correct khatian and correctly recorded at the trial court but it was alleged to be wrong only before the court of appeal below and the court rightly rejected that contention to be not considerable at the appellate stage. At the trial plaintiff No. 1 being P.W. 1 son of Shasi Daradi one of the original tenant had said that he had 2 and 5 annas and odd share in Khatian No. 444 and 929 which is the recording of the khatian. This being the case he may not be allowed to find a new case at the appellate stage. Defendannt also claimed that the khatians are correctly recorded, and in that view of the matter the court found the khatian correctly recorded with cogent reasons which I find reason to interfere in this appeal which is also not agitated before this Court. P.W. 1 stated before the trial court that he had 1/3rd share in khatian No. 764 and in that view of the matter the court rightly found that Jadunath had interest to the extent of .27, Feli .27, Khudiram and his to the extent of .27, Feli .27 Khudiram and his brother .27, and Shasi .17 in the Khas land under khatian No. 444 covering an area of 1.64 and the same is the case with the khas land of khatian No. 929 covering an area 2.84. It is seen on a reference to khatian No. 444 that Jadunath there in had been clearly recorded as a tenant having a share of more than 4 annas of the total area of 8.44 decimal covered by that khatian but he was recorded to be not in possession in the column kept for recording possession against the plot number. It is seen that those were possessed by Shasi Daradi, Khudiram and Feli and other 3 Riyats holding tenancy under Jamindary of Mohammad Shahi under Touji No. 178 appertaining to Mohammad Shahi Parganas within mouza Putimari, District Jessore. Jadu Nath therefore, is a recorded tenant along with other 3 tenants who are predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiff and also of the defendant because in this case the defendants were claiming through Feli Bewa and plaintiffs claiming through Shasi and Khudiram son of Kartic.
